info.name: Nexmile — Rider App
info.description:
Rider authentication and onboarding for the Flutter app.

**Authentication is identical to the customer app**, with one difference: send `"intended_role": "rider"` when requesting the first code. That is the only auth difference between the two apps.

**A rider is not active after signing in.** The account is created as `pending` and stays that way until an admin verifies their documents. Onboarding is therefore a wizard, not a single screen:

1. Sign in by OTP
2. Fill in profile and document numbers
3. Upload six documents
4. Submit for verification
5. Wait for an admin decision
6. Only then can the rider go on duty

Build for the case where the rider closes the app halfway through — `GET /rider/kyc` returns exactly what is still missing, so the wizard can resume from the right step.

request.description:
`intended_role: "rider"` only matters the first time this identifier signs in — it decides what kind of account gets created. Sending it on later sign-ins is harmless.

Swap `email` for `phone` once SMS is live.

exec: console.log('Signed in · status', d.user.status, '— KYC required before going on duty');

request.description: Returns `user.status = "pending"`. Unlike a customer, the rider **cannot work yet** — route them into the onboarding wizard, not the home screen.
Serialise refreshes behind one lock. Concurrent refreshes are treated as a stolen token and revoke every session.

exec: console.log('KYC:', d.status, '· missing:', d.missing_documents.join(', ') || 'nothing', '· can submit:', d.can_submit);

request.description:
**Call this on every app launch and after every upload.** It returns:

- `status` — `pending`, `submitted`, `verified` or `rejected`
- `missing_documents` — exactly what still needs uploading
- `can_submit` — whether the Submit button should be enabled
- `documents[]` — each with its own `status` and `rejection_reason`
- `rejection_reason` — set when an admin rejected the whole account

Drive the wizard entirely from this response rather than tracking progress locally: the rider may switch devices, and an admin may reject a document after submission.

The numbers printed on the documents. All fields optional — send whichever the rider has filled in so far.

Validation: Aadhaar 12 digits, PAN `ABCDE1234F`, IFSC `HDFC0001234`, and both expiry dates must be in the future.

**Returns 422 once KYC is verified.** An approved rider cannot swap in a different licence, so lock these fields in the UI when `status` is `verified`.

formdata.description: aadhaar_front | aadhaar_back | pan_card | driving_licence | vehicle_rc | vehicle_insurance | bank_proof | profile_photo
JPG, PNG or PDF, up to 5 MB

request.description:
**`multipart/form-data`, not JSON.** Do not set a Content-Type header by hand — the HTTP client sets the boundary.

Six types are required:
`aadhaar_front`, `aadhaar_back`, `pan_card`, `driving_licence`, `vehicle_rc`, `vehicle_insurance`.

Optional: `bank_proof`, `profile_photo`.

Re-uploading a type replaces the previous file, so "retake photo" needs no delete first.

Returns 422 if that type was already **approved** — approved documents are locked.

Compress camera images before upload: a modern phone photo can exceed the 5 MB limit.
Only while pending or rejected. Approved documents return 422.

Moves the account to `submitted`.

Returns 422 listing what is missing if any required document is absent — check `can_submit` first and keep the button disabled until it is true.

After this, show a waiting screen. Verification is a manual admin decision, usually within two working days.

Includes `can_accept_orders` — the single flag to gate the whole working UI on. It is true only when KYC is verified, documents are unexpired, and the rider is on duty.

Also returns `documents_expired`, so the app can warn before a licence lapses.

`vehicle_type` is `bicycle`, `motorcycle`, `scooter` or `ev`.

Riders must be at least 18 — an earlier date of birth returns 422.

Accepts `available`, `offline` or `on_break`.

`on_order` is set by dispatch and is rejected here.

**Returns 403 if KYC is not verified, or if the licence or insurance has expired.** The message explains which — show it rather than a generic error, since the rider can act on it.

Going offline always works, whatever the KYC state.
